transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jonas (Redwood Product), Jordan (AcuityCare CTO), Priya (ML Lead), Evan (Infra), Sofia (PM)

[00:00] Samir: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Samir, AE on the account, and with me is Maya our systems SE and Jonas on product. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Jordan: Good, Samir. Thanks. We're excited to see the "decision matrix" you mentioned for precision profiles. We've been kicking tires on INT8 internally but worried about regressions.
[00:22] Maya: Great — today we'll use the Optimize console to walk through a decision matrix that maps workload signals to recommended precision profiles, show an INT8 vs FP8 demo, and outline a pilot. I will walk the console and show the live benchmark dashboards.
[00:35] Priya: Awesome. For context, our primary workload is conversational triage with ~700 token average prompts, some longer context. Latency p95 needs to be < 400ms for the RU service; accuracy drop >2% on our intent classification is a no-go.
[00:50] Evan: And infra constraints: we want VPC deployment, KMS-integration, and ability to fall back to hosted endpoints if private capacity gets saturated.
[01:02] Maya: Noted. We'll highlight how rollouts and automatic fallback work in the console. Quick note — I might mispronounce a couple of names or say "Redwood Optima" today, sorry, transcription will be messy.

-- Console walkthrough / Decision matrix --

[01:20] Maya: Opening the Optimize console — top left is the "Decision Matrix" tab. The matrix shows rows for request characteristics (avg tokens, prompt variance, latency SLO, cost sensitivity) and columns with profile recommendations: FP16 baseline, FP8 for latency-sensitive medium-fidelity, INT8 aggressive for high-throughput low-cost.
[01:40] Jonas: The idea is to convert telemetry (p50/p95 latencies, token distribution, cache hit rates) into a score for each axis and pick the profile with the best expected utility.
[01:55] Priya: How do you quantify "quality"? Our metrics are a mix — intent accuracy, top-1 classification, and some manual human evals.
[02:05] Maya: We support custom quality metrics. For the demo I'm using a proxy: intent F1 and a small human-eval sample (n=200). In the matrix you can weight metrics — e.g., 70% quality, 30% cost — and the console will surface profiles that meet SLOs.

[02:20] -- INT8 vs FP8 live sample --

[02:22] Maya: Alright now I'm switching to the bench tab. I have two model variants deployed: med-chat-fp8 and med-chat-int8 (note: avatars in the UI say "med-chat-fp8"; in our internal docs we sometimes call them fp8-lite). We'll run a 10-minute synthetic load that mirrors your token distribution.
[02:40] [02:40] (background: clicking sounds)
[02:45] Maya: Starting run. First glance at throughput — INT8 gains about 2.6x tokens/sec in these nodes. p50 for FP8 sits at ~120ms, INT8 p50 ~75ms. p95 for FP8 is 310ms, INT8 is 260ms in this synthetic test.
[03:12] Jordan: Those p95 numbers are promising, but what's the quality delta?
[03:16] Maya: Good question. On the intent F1, FP8 is at 0.957, INT8 is at 0.945 in this run — that's about a 1.2% absolute drop. On the small human eval, we flagged specific failure modes: hallucination on rare entities and subtle phrasing changes.
[03:36] Priya: That's in line with what we feared. Our threshold was 2% absolute, so that would pass. But we care about edge-case pharma names — did you see name corruption?
[03:46] Maya: We did. A few brand names were shortened or slightly scrambled in INT8 runs. For those we'd recommend a hybrid: keep FP8 for prompts flagged as high-risk (entity-sensitive) and route bulk traffic to INT8. That's where the decision matrix helps.

[04:05] -- Routing and rollouts --

[04:08] Maya: In the console I'll show a canary rollout. You can configure per-route policies: e.g., 10% traffic to INT8, 90% FP8, monitor quality dashboards and auto-rollback on regression >1.5% in your metric. Also built-in prefix/KV caching reduces delta for high-similarity prompts.
[04:33] Evan: For VPC/private: if we do a hybrid routing policy, do we need separate capacity pools for INT8 and FP8?
[04:40] Jonas: Yes, different quantization profiles may use different instance types or kernel sets; in Dedicated/Private you can reserve both pools and set autoscale policies. Default fallback is configured so if INT8 pool is full, traffic shifts to FP8 or to hosted.

[05:00] -- Cost discussion --

[05:03] Samir: Quick cost model: INT8 typically reduces per-token GPU cost by ~40-60% depending on hardware and batch efficiency. FP8 sits between FP16 and INT8. The Optimize console shows estimated monthly spend delta given your token volume — I have a cost projection for AcuityCare in the docs link I will share.
[05:23] Priya: Can that projection include the cost of extra checkpoints / eval runs? We run a lot of held-out evals.
[05:29] Maya: Yes, you can add eval job budgets as a line item; the decision matrix can factor in eval cadence. Also we can run a smoke-run of your held-out set during the pilot for baseline comparison.

[05:48] -- Technical deep dive (kernel selection, KV cache) --

[05:50] Maya: On the runtime side, kernel selection chooses optimized kernels based on sequence length and model arch. We use continuous batching and KV cache coalescing to maintain latency while increasing throughput. I mentioned earlier you might see "K-V cash" in some transcriptions — it's KV cache, not cash.
[06:06] Evan: For private deployment, what about KMS/HSM? We need to ensure keys never leave our control.
[06:12] Jonas: We support KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for the Private control plane. Audit logs are available and the console will show per-request tracing hooks if you enable them. We also have SOC2 Type II evidence in the security pack.

[06:34] -- Benchmark anomalies and sensitivity tests --

[06:36] Maya: During the run we saw a small number of outliers — a few INT8 responses at p95 slipped to 420ms in a node with high GC. We flagged those as infra-induced, not model-quality issues. For quality sensitivity, the console will run a sweep: incrementally apply INT8 perturbations and compute degradation curves for your metric.
[06:56] Priya: How fine-grained is the qprofile? Can we do mixed precision inside a single model (e.g., critical attention layers FP8, others INT8)?
[07:05] Maya: We support mixed precision profiles at the compilation level — it's part of the qprofile. The Optimize UI surfaces recommended layer-level configs for high-risk workloads. This is more advanced but often yields the best cost/quality tradeoff.

[07:25] -- Canary live results and dashboard --

[07:26] Maya: I'm toggling canary now to 15% INT8 for a sample route. Look at the dashboard: quality delta is shown over time with rolling 30-minute windows. We set an alert to pause the rollout if intent F1 drops more than 1.5%.
[07:45] Jordan: If the alert trips, is rollback instantaneous?
[07:49] Maya: It's automated; we do a weighted rollback over 30 seconds to avoid amplifying transient spikes. You can also set manual approval gates.

[08:02] -- Customer-specific concerns --

[08:04] Evan: Network egress between our VPC and Redwood private instances — we need clarity on peering and audit of IP ranges for firewall rules.
[08:12] Samir: We'll share a network diagram and the peering checklist. Also, if you want a fully air-gapped on-prem install, we can discuss that under our Private offering — it's a separate contract.
[08:24] Sofia: On SLAs — we need p95 latency and uptime commitments for the dedicated pool. What do you typically offer?
[08:31] Jonas: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets that can be part of the reserved capacity contract. We'll include draft SLA language in the packet Samir sends.

[08:44] -- Evals and human-in-the-loop --

[08:46] Priya: We want to include periodic human evals during pilot and tie regressions to a reviewer queue. Can Optimize surface examples that failed so we can triage?
[08:55] Maya: Yes — failed prompts are sampled and shown with diff views. You can create postmortem tickets with attached examples, and the console links to the rollout timeline for correlation.

[09:10] -- Data residency & retention --

[09:12] Jordan: Data residency: we store logs in-region for EU customers. For us, do you offer retention policies and deletion APIs?
[09:19] Jonas: Region-based retention, deletion APIs, and configurable log redaction are available in Private/Dedicated. Hosted customers have tenancy options but we can scope retention to meet compliance. We'll surface the exact policies in the security pack.

[09:32] Samir: Quick housekeeping — we'll share the deck and the Optimize decision-matrix template after the call. Any other questions before we cover the pilot plan?

[09:40] Sofia: Timeline — we want a pilot that runs with production-like traffic for two weeks and includes a final run of our evaluation set. Are you able to support that cadence?
[09:48] Maya: Yes. Our suggested plan: week 0 — sandbox setup + baseline collection; week 1 — incremental quantized rollouts (10%, 25%, 50%); week 2 — steady-state at chosen profile with stress testing and final eval. We'll provide benchmark sheets you can fill.

[10:05] -- Pilot logistics and acceptance criteria --

[10:07] Samir: Acceptance criteria proposed: 1) Intent F1 drop <= 2% absolute vs baseline; 2) p95 latency < 400ms; 3) no high-severity hallucination events on the held-out set (SLA to define). If all pass, we move to reserved capacity planning.
[10:24] Priya: We want the decision matrix exported as a CSV we can version in our repo. Can we get that?
[10:29] Maya: Yep — export and API access available. We'll also provide a CLI tool to apply qprofiles to your infra during the pilot.

[10:40] -- Pricing and procurement --

[10:42] Samir: On pricing — pilot pricing is usage-based with an option to convert to a reserved commit for Dedicated. I'll include a pilot quote plus the committed pricing for both FP8 and INT8 pools.
[10:52] Jordan: Procurement — legal will need SOC2 docs and terms. Who do we talk to on your side?
[10:57] Samir: I'll loop in our legal and security team, and share the security pack. Expect SOC2 Type II and data processing addendum in the next email.

[11:10] -- Quick live trouble-shoot: an oddity --

[11:12] Maya: Small note — in the synthetic run there was a corner-case where the INT8 decoder produced a truncated token on long sequences. We re-ran with a different kernel and it resolved. Kernel selection sometimes needs a manual nudge for very long contexts.
[11:28] Priya: So we should include a long-context test in our eval set.
[11:31] Maya: Absolutely — include samples >2000 tokens.

[11:36] -- Closing recap --

[11:38] Samir: Recap: we'll run a two-week sandbox pilot, Maya shares the matrix template and benchmark sheet, Priya will upload prompt sets, Evan to confirm VPC peering and KMS, and I will send pricing/SLA draft.
[11:52] Jordan: Sounds good — we'll aim to get the prompt sets and infra sign-off by Friday.
[11:58] Samir: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the kickoff.

[12:05] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings ("K-V cash" instead of "KV cache", "Optima" for Optimize), filler words and overlaps present.
